body: The selector values are the ones the emitter names in `codex/compiler/Emit/X86_64Boot.codex`. A program reaches the builtin rather than the compiler's constants, so they are spelled again here.

author: val
body: One request's headers and body. The same 64 KiB the bare-metal server caps a receive at, for the same reason: it is one request, not a stream budget.

author: val
body: The bytes on the wire are UNICODE octets, not CCE, exactly as they are for the bare-metal server: `http-parse-request` and `http-encode` own that conversion, so nothing here converts anything.

author: val
body: A SHORT SEND IS NOT A SENT RESPONSE. `send` answers how many bytes it took, and a partial write leaves the client reading a body that stops mid-stream, so the loop keeps offering the remainder until the whole response is gone or the call refuses. The bare-metal server closes on a short send for the same reason, stated in `WebServer`: a half-written response cannot be repaired.
